item.title: Kremlin aide denies US assertion that Europeans will join next round of Ukraine peace talks
item.description: MOSCOW, Nov 16 (Reuters) - A senior Kremlin aide said on Monday that Russia had not yet agreed to the participation of European representatives in the next round of Ukraine peace talks, contradicting comments by US negotiators after talks in Moscow that the Europeans would be atthe next negotiations.

item.title: After Yemen setback, Saudi Arabia replaces military commander
item.description:
By Timour Azhari and Mohammed Ghobari

RIYADH, Nov 16 (Reuters) - Saudi Arabia replaced the commander overseeing its coalition against Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on Monday after Riyadh's Yemeni allies were forced to withdraw from swathes of territory in a major setback for their campaign against the group.

The Houthis have made rapid gains against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government sincethe US-Iran conflict reignited Yemen's frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group.

item.title: First draft of COP31 deal signals tough negotiations to come
item.description:
By Simon Jessop and Sarah McFarlane

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 16 (Reuters) - Negotiators at COP31 talks in Turkey published a draft deal text on Monday to drive debate and try to narrow the gaps between countries over fossil fuels and climate financing ahead of an end-of-week deadline to forge a final agreement.

The stakes are high after a year of global warming that has caused wildfires in Europe and a deadly glacier melt in Nepal, while political will for action is undermined by other crises, including wars and the rising cost of living.

item.title: Iranian leaders fret over public mood as gas shortages add to war ills
item.description:
By Parisa Hafezi and Melory Ghazi

DUBAI, Nov 16 (Reuters) - Iran shows no sign of making concessions in the war with the US, but its warnings to citizens of gas shortages this winter are the latest sign of its own vulnerabilities in the conflict, with its ports blockaded and infrastructure hammered by US strikes.

The government said last week that, though Iran has had gas shortages before, they would be more severe this winter because of war damage to processing plants and most regions would be affected.

item.title: Iran’s proxy in Iraq rakes in hundreds of millions through oil smuggling
item.description:
By Ahmed Rasheed

BAGHDAD, Nov 16 (Reuters) - Iran's most powerful Shi'ite militia ally in Iraq has been raking in hundreds of millions of dollars from oil stolen from the state, Iraqi officials say, prompting the prime minister to ready his security forces to confront the heavily armed group.

Prime Minister Alial-Zaidi has launched his toughest challenge yet to the group Kataib Hezbollah by cracking down on an oil smuggling network it has run for years, senior security, army, police and oil officials told Reuters.

item.title: UN ready to support any denuclearisation effort from US, China, Russia talks
item.description:
By Mikhail Flores and Nestor Corrales

MANILA, Nov 16 (Reuters) - TheUnited Nations is prepared to support anydenuclearisation effort that may arise from this week's summit meeting of China, Russia and the United States, UN chief Antonio Guterres said on Monday,despite a lack of certainty about such an outcome.

"If there is a denuclearisation program, we are ready to be fully engaged in that and contribute to make it a success," UN Secretary-General Guterres said in Manila, where he is attending a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

item.title: US Democrats bring hope of climate comeback to COP31
item.description:
By Valerie Volcovici

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The United States officially is absent from COP31. But on the ground at the climate talks on the Turkish Mediterranean coast, its presence is hard to miss.

Emboldened by the Democrats' congressional election victories this month, US lawmakers, governors and former officials have packed venues across the climate summit. They have promised the US will return to the Paris climate agreement "with humility" and they say climate action is alive despite President Donald Trump.

item.title: Jordan and Iraq block Telegram app over national security concerns
item.description:
Nov 16 (Reuters) - Jordanian and Iraqi authorities said on Monday they will block the Telegram social media service for national security reasons, with Baghdad's media regulator saying the app had not done enough to stop offending content.

The Public Security Directorate in Jordan — a US ally in the fight against militants — said it wanted to guard against "attempts to spread extremism and radicalisation".
